newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian premier sees more cooperation with Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Indian premier sees more cooperation with Pakistan.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Saturday he expected more areas of cooperation with arch-rival Pakistan to emerge at a rare summit meeting in May following recent high-level talks between the two countries.

"When I look at the past few weeks gone by, I think India-Pakistan relationships have improved a great deal," Gujral, who was foreign minister until taking office as prime minister last Monday, told Reuters.
"Now, as prime minister, when I meet Mr Nawaz Sharif in Male, I will resume links, and I think we are moving towards discovering more and more areas of cooperation."

Gujral and Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif are expected to meet next month in the Maldivian capital city of Male on the fringes of a summit of the seven-nation South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC).
"Though we may not agree on all issues, we see a wide range of subjects on which we believe we can collaborate effectively," Gujral said in a letter to Sharif earlier this week.
Gujral was sworn in as prime minister on Monday to head a new government formed by the United Front coalition which changed its leader under a political deal with the Congress party.
The Congress on April 11 toppled the 10-month-old government headed by H.D. Deve Gowda.

Gujral said talks held between senior civil servants of the two countries in March, and his own meeting with Pakistan's Foreign Minister, Gohar Ayub Khan, in April in New Delhi had prepared the ground for more cooperation.

Official talks were resumed in March after a three-year gap, after a previous round in 1994 broke down over Kashmir, the disputed region which has brought the two neighbours to war three times since independence in 1947.

As foreign minister, the new prime minister promoted what has come to be called the "Gujral doctrine", saying a large nation like India can afford to offer unilateral concessions without reciprocity in order to boost neighbourly relations.
